featured_reviews.name: kavita bekal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I usually write reviews when I truly like a place, but I felt the need to share this experience because my stomach was upset after eating here, which is concerning.

I visited this restaurant expecting authentic Ratnagiri/Konkan food, especially given the name and the 4-star rating. Unfortunately, the food did not meet those expectations at all.

I ordered a fish thali, but there was nothing about it that reflected true Konkan or Ratnagiri cuisine. The fish fry was bland, not properly marinated, and lacked basic flavor. I had to add salt, pepper, and lime myself just to make it edible. Authentic Konkan fish fry is known for its seasoning and marinade, which was completely missing here.

The fish curry was a simple onion-based gravy with no depth—no kokum, no tamarind, no spice, and not even the correct color of a traditional fish curry. The thali included bhakri, rice, fish fry, fish curry, sol curry, and a dry fish preparation. Except for the dry item, nothing tasted authentic or satisfying.

I also ordered chicken sukka, which is supposed to be dry and at least mildly spicy. What was served was more like a regular chicken curry with gravy, not dry at all, and completely lacking spice and flavor. It did not resemble chicken sukka in any way.

I had high expectations, but the food was nowhere near what one would expect from a place claiming to serve Ratnagiri or Konkan cuisine. This food does not represent Konkan food, not even remotely.

Overall, a very disappointing experience, and due to both the quality of the food and the health issue afterward, I would not recommend this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last evening, visited O Pedro at Godrej BKC to catch up with friends, and overall it turned out to be a lively and enjoyable experience. The restaurant definitely has a strong personality of its own — vibrant ambience, energetic crowd, good music, and a stylish Goan-Latin inspired vibe that makes it feel different from the usual BKC dining places.

The ambience and overall vibe are honestly one of the biggest strengths of O Pedro. The place feels warm, colourful, and social without becoming too loud or chaotic. It’s ideal for group outings and long conversations over food and drinks. The interiors are beautifully done, and the energy of the place keeps the atmosphere upbeat throughout the evening.

Coming to the food and drinks, we ordered quite a variety.

The Stranger & Sons cocktail was refreshing and smooth with balanced botanical flavours. It paired really well with the starters.

The Crab Ros Omelette was flavourful and rich, with soft eggs wrapped around well-seasoned crab filling. It had a comforting yet indulgent taste.

The Malaki Indian Tonic was light, crisp, and refreshing, making it a good accompaniment during the meal.

The Guava Pineapple Sour had a tropical sweetness balanced nicely with a sour finish. Refreshing and enjoyable without being overly sweet.

The Choriz Chilly Fry (Gluten Free) was one of the highlights. Packed with bold Goan flavours, smoky spice, and excellent texture, it paired wonderfully with drinks.

The Grilled Chicken Peri Peri was juicy and well-marinated with balanced heat levels. The chicken was cooked properly without drying out.

The Picante Highballin cocktail had a nice spicy-citrus profile and worked very well for those who enjoy slightly stronger flavours.

The All Poee Basket and freshly served Poee were excellent accompaniments. Soft, fresh, and authentic, they complemented the spicy dishes beautifully.

The Cardoz’s Chicken Chilli Fry had strong coastal flavours with a nice spice kick. The preparation felt rustic and flavourful.

The Monkey Shoulder (60ml) was smooth and enjoyable as expected for whisky lovers.

The Roasted Lamb Chops were tender, juicy, and cooked well. The seasoning was balanced and allowed the flavour of the meat to stand out nicely.

We ended with Aunty Li’s Serradura, which was creamy, light, and a perfect dessert to finish the meal without feeling too heavy.

The staff throughout the evening was courteous, attentive, and helpful. Service was fairly smooth despite the restaurant being busy.

However, there were a few things that slightly impacted the overall experience.

The first was the extremely high cover charge for confirmed bookings. Charging ₹1,000 per person through food apps for securing a preferred time slot felt excessive, even though the amount gets adjusted in the final bill. Most restaurants usually charge somewhere between ₹50–₹250 for reservation commitments, so ₹1,000 per head honestly feels unnecessarily high.

Secondly, while the food quality was good, some dishes did feel slightly overpriced and somewhat overhyped considering the portion sizes and overall value.

Another small drawback was that towards the later part of the evening, there seemed to be subtle pressure to vacate the table for the next guests. While understandable from an operational perspective, it could definitely have been handled in a more polished and guest-friendly manner, especially when people are dining and catching up socially.

That said, the overall experience was still enjoyable because of the good vibes, lively ambience, flavourful food, and pleasant company. O Pedro is definitely a place worth visiting at least once for its atmosphere and unique menu.

Overall, a good experience with some room for improvement in guest handling and pricing balance. Great for catching up with friends and enjoying a vibrant evening in BKC.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sharing my honest and no filter review. Visited this place with my friend on Tuesday, 9th June after filtering Sai Palace out.
We went on a weekday and unfortunately the tandoor wasn't available from Monday to Friday. It was disheartening to hear tha bcz we wanted to order prawns tandoori. Now that we had already sat on the table we tried to run through the Food Menu. I asked the server, for possible options in non veg starters since tandoor wasn't available and I was surprised to hear that Ghee roast is a starter item and not a main course. On asking the reason the server responded that at Nav Gomantak they treat it as starters. None the less we ordered Prawns Ghee Roast and Bombil Fry. Prawns were 80% cooked and bombil fry had no salt and taste. One word "pathetic". For main course we ordered Chulvarcha mutton and Jeera rice and i was surprised to hear Chulvarcha Mutton (mutton prepared on coal/wood fire) is prepared on gas they has just named it Chulvarcha. Again below average taste mostly over Burnt. Could taste the burnt masala rather than fried. We couldn't finish the mutton and hers rice and packed it and took it with us.
Next day my mother ate the mutton dish and she too said the same thing.
So the restaurant is over hyped. The food is no influence of malvani cuisine let alone Goan cuisine. Spent 2000 for the food, experience 3/10.
Fancy seats, bright lightings or good looking cutlery doesn't guarantee you good and VFM food is what Nav Gomantak taught us. Skipping this restaurant forever. Hope the owners read my comment and improve the food quality.
The 4.3 rating is just a scam

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Something’s Fishy last week to celebrate a family friend’s birthday.

If you’re a seafood lover, Something’s Fishy is the kind of place that instantly feels right. From the moment you step in, the ambience sets the mood. The interiors have a beautiful seafood-inspired theme, artistically done without being over the top. Subtle marine elements, thoughtful décor, and warm lighting make the space feel relaxed and inviting. It’s comfortable enough for a family dinner yet stylish enough for a special outing.

We tried quite a variety of dishes, and honestly, the experience from start to finish was satisfying.

Harra Channa ka Shorba (Chicken Soup): A comforting, mildly spiced chicken soup with fresh herb flavours. Light yet flavourful, it had a soothing warmth and well-balanced seasoning, perfect to begin the meal.

Chicken Gassi: Rich, coastal-style chicken curry with aromatic spices and creamy coconut base. The gravy was flavourful without being overpowering, and the chicken pieces were tender and well-cooked.

Appams: Soft, fluffy appams with delicate crisp edges. Light texture and subtle sweetness paired beautifully with the gassi gravies, soaking up flavours perfectly without becoming soggy.

Prawn Gassi: Fresh prawns cooked in traditional coastal gravy with coconut and spices. The prawns were juicy and tender, absorbing the rich masala while retaining their natural sweetness.

Butter Garlic Prawn: Perfectly sautéed prawns tossed in butter and garlic. Simple yet delicious, with a lovely aroma and balanced seasoning that allowed the freshness of the seafood to shine.

Surmai Fry: Crispy on the outside, moist and flaky inside. The fish was fresh, well-marinated, and fried just right, delivering bold coastal flavours without excessive oiliness.

Rawas Tandoori: Well-marinated rawas grilled to perfection in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, and packed with spices, yet the fish remained soft and flavourful inside.

Squid Crispy Fried Rings: Lightly battered squid rings fried till crisp. Crunchy outside, tender inside, with balanced seasoning that made them addictive without feeling too heavy.

What stood out throughout the meal was the freshness of the seafood. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, not rushed. Portions were generous, and the flavours felt authentic rather than overly commercialised.

Service was smooth and friendly. The staff were attentive, happy to recommend dishes, and ensured everything was served at the right pace. They didn’t hover unnecessarily, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, Something’s Fishy delivers exactly what you expect from a seafood speciality restaurant — fresh ingredients, authentic coastal flavours, and a warm, pleasant ambience. It’s definitely a place I’d revisit whenever seafood cravings strike. Highly recommended for anyone who truly enjoys well-prepared seafood.

We ordered the paan style surmai that was wrapped in a banana leaf and roasted, the sukha bhujane prawns and the crab soup. featured_reviews.name: Ralph Pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dishes we had:
1. Crab Lollipop: 6/10
2. Thalis with Rice Bhakaris
-a. Surmai: 10/10
-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10
3. Gulab Jamun: 3/10
4. Fresh Lime Soda: 8/10

Crab Lollipop wasn't great. I have had better elsewhere.
It lacked the basic crab taste and the coating too was very mild on flavor.

The thalis were awesome. The fish were very fresh and tasty that it made our day. Surmai was the best. It had the best flavor, followed by Pomfret and then the Bombil. Surmai and Pomfret were rawa fry with little masala. It was just plain batter fry for the Bombil. We make better Bombil fry at home, so yeah.
The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

featured_reviews.name: Yogen Sachdev
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally revisited Maaslli – Saraswat and GSB Speciality last night for my annual catch-up with friends, and once again, it reminded me why this place is rightly awarded the best seafood restaurant in Mumbai.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back.

Maaslli Restaurant & Bar, at Kemps Corner, Mumbai.
Basically a Sea food Restaurant, but also have other non veg dishes on their platter.
One cannot afford to miss the fried Bombil (Fresh, Fried Bombay Ducks).
They have a great Menu.
They do have various Thali dishes and other alcarte dishes.
It is just mouth watering and thus unable to put in words to describe the dishes.
One must enjoy the crab dishes and crab soup.
They also present you their fresh catch and you may select the fish if your choice, depending upon the weight the rate is fixed.
The atmosphere is damn cool and decent with fishes reflecting in the walls and partisans.
The curry, different types is served and we are asked to taste, then by adding coconut oil again to try. Thus if you are ordering any curry dish you can select your choice of curry.
The staff is very courteous and friendly.

featured_reviews.name: vidisha pisal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The restaurant covers India’s west + southwest coast, plus Kerala. All of them are big on seafood, coconut, and bold spices but each has its own vibe

- *Mangalorean*: Known for fiery, coconut-heavy curries and _ghee roast_. Uses Byadagi chilies for color + flavor. Lots of pork, seafood, and kori roti.
- *Malvani*: From Maharashtra’s Konkan belt. Dry coconut, kokum, and tirphal/sichuan pepper give it a tangy, peppery kick. Famous for fish curries and thalis.
- *Konkan/Goan*: Coconut + kokum again, but Goan food also has Portuguese influence — vindaloo, cafreal, and lots of vinegar. Seafood + pork are staples.
- *Kerala*: Coconut oil, curry leaves, black pepper, and rice-based sides like appam and puttu. Big on fish, beef, and subtle but complex spice.

*The Ambience & Service*
- *Ambience*: When a place calls itself “one of the finest” with coastal food, expect warm lighting, usually means clean, spacious, not too loud.
- *Staff*: “Very generous” usually means attentive service, good portion sizes, and staff who’ll guide you through the menu if you’re new to coastal food.

### *The Food — Dish by Dish*

*Starters / Tandoor*
- *Tandoor Soya Chaap*: Soya chunks marinated in curd, ginger-garlic, and tandoori masala, then charred in the tandoor. Smoky, juicy, with that red tandoori exterior. Great veg option that mimics kebabs.
- *Prawns Ghee Roast*: A Mangalorean classic. Prawns tossed in a thick, caramelized masala of ghee, Byadagi + red chilies, garlic, and curry leaves.

*Mains / Thalis*
- *Surmai Thali*: _Surmai_ = Kingfish/Seer fish. A thali means a full plate: fried or curry surmai as the hero, plus rice/bhakri, solkadi, a veg side, pickle, and sometimes a prawns or clams sukka. Coastal thalis are all about balance — spicy fish, cooling solkadi, and rice.
- *Mutton Thali*:Kolhapuri style mutton. Dark, spicy curry with dagad phool and dry coconut, fall-off-bone meat. Comes with bhakri or vade, rice, and sides. Hearty and peppery.
- *Kori Roti with Curry*: Mangalorean comfort food. _Kori_ = chicken curry with a thin, red, coconut-based gravy. _Roti_ = not wheat roti but crisp, dry rice wafers that you crush and soak in the curry. It goes from crunchy to soft in seconds.
- *Neer Dosa*: From coastal Karnataka. _Neer_ = water. Paper-thin, soft, lacy dosa made from just rice batter. No fermentation, so it’s mild and perfect for mopping up spicy ghee roast or chicken curry.
- *Appam*: Kerala’s bowl-shaped rice + coconut pancake. Crispy lacy edges, soft spongy center. Made for sopping up stew or curry.
- *Surmai Garlic Tawa Fry*: Thick surmai steak marinated in chili-garlic paste, rava or rice flour coating, then shallow-fried on a tawa. Spicy, garlicky, crusty outside and flaky inside.

*Mocktails*
- *Green Valley Mocktail
- *Lovely Smile Mocktail
*Dessert*
- *Gadbad*: Mangalore’s iconic ice cream sundae. Translates to “hurry-scurry”. Served in a tall glass with layers of 3-4 ice cream flavors, jelly, fresh fruit, dry fruits, and nuts. Chaotic, colorful, and meant to be mixed as you eat.

basically did a coastal crawl in one meal — tandoor for smoky start, ghee roast + tawa fry for spice, thalis for the full experience, and neer dosa/appam/kori roti to try all the classic carb pairings. Then cooled it down with mocktails and ended with Mangalore’s most famous dessert.

Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

featured_reviews.name: Deep Sett
featured_reviews.review_text:
TOTALLY AVOID WASTING RS 5000.

At the onset this is probably one of the most expensive Buffets you would be having in Mumbai, priced at over 4300 plus taxes for a Dinner on a Weekday for an adult. Add to that, even as a gold accor member you probably get 20-30 percent instead of the normal 50 percent for 2 people is taxing.

The spread is decent, the variety in principal is there, but in terms of the taste and the quality of food, it’s really one of the poorest of the five stars , even considering the Leela and Lalit brands in Mumbai whose lay is very modest compared to this.

At almost 5000 you expect
1. Your veg sushi not being dumped in the refrigerator for you to pick up, questioning when it was made !

2. No juice , cold drink or mocktails are part of this offering. An advise to the team, you’re charging 5000 offering a drink probably at times could feel better than half the items on the menu.

3. I have seen just one Langarwaali daal the last 4 times I have gone here, to be honest , a Dal Makhani is the norm, if not that a top of the line dal Tadka.

4. Some dishes are borderline tasteless and on the menu just to increase the offerings on paper / website
A. Sushi - cold, refrigerated, and tasted as if it was made with zero interest.
B. Pizza Margerita- looked like an Udipi version not one served at a top 5 star, see the pictures yourself.
C. Fattoush salad, I mean if anyone has had a look at what they serve with that name, it’s embarrassing.
D. Starters like paneer tikka seem like lying there unattended for hours.
E. Many of the deserts too seem just good looking and tasting on borderline just sugar toffees.

When you come to a place , the stature of a Sofitel From the ACCOR elite stable, you expect basic standards and taste but unfortunately that’s missing.

The fact that it’s in BKC and most people have very little options for a 5 Star experience, plus because of its location the occupancy is high, is the best answer to why it’s half full during these buffets otherwise as per the taste of the food it should be  probably amongst the slowest moving places ever.

Sofitel I have over 11 million people reading this, so I’m saying this with humility please pull up and improve , make prices more competitive and the food seem like it’s made with care for the guests and hopefully the most charm would be back.

Till then all the best!!

Had a wonderful dining experience at Big Fish & Co, Dadar! We started with Bharlela Bombil and Chicken Pepper Fry, both packed with authentic coastal flavors. The Raw Mango Cooler, Kokan Kanya (kokum-based drink), and Sol Kadhi were refreshing and perfectly complemented the meal.

The only downside is that parking can be quite difficult to find around the restaurant. Apart from that, the overall experience was very good. Would definitely visit again!

The food was really good and the ambience was pleasant, making it a nice place to relax and enjoy a meal. Service was also good and the staff were courteous.
One thing to note — the restaurant mentions parking availability, but parking can be difficult since the place is quite inside from the main road.
Other than that, everything was good and worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: chinu's kitchen
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited The Big Fish & Co. on 4th January while I was shopping around Dadar with my mom and sister. While shopping nearby, we asked a local person for a good restaurant recommendation, and she suggested this place — and honestly, it turned out to be a great choice.
Right from the entrance, the experience was pleasant. The security guard at the door was very polite and kind. He asked if we had a reservation (we didn’t), but luckily a few tables were available. Since we were just three people, we were seated comfortably without any wait.
The ambience is quite good — warm, comfortable, and very suitable for families and friends. There were absolutely no negative points when it came to the atmosphere. What really touched my heart was the attentiveness of the staff. They listened carefully, were patient, and ensured everything was smooth. The service was quick, with no unnecessary delays, which I truly appreciated.
Coming to the food — it felt very local and authentic, something I personally connect with. The dishes were unique and well-prepared. We ordered tandoori prawns, which were medium-sized and nicely cooked. I also ordered a thali and a crab dish, both of which were absolutely delicious and the dessert tooo it’s new for me being a konkani
Overall, it was worth the visit. Great food, warm service, and a lovely atmosphere. I truly loved the experience and would definitely recommend this place.
